text:
aj: Heads up — since this morning we're seeing intermittent gRPC streaming stalls between pods in us-west-2a -> us-west-2b. Inference pods (gpu-serving) hang on long-lived streams, CPU is fine but GPUs show queue buildup.
Maria: saw the alerts. Any correlation with recent infra changes?
aj: We rolled a NIC firmware update on the west fleet yesterday and bumped kernel on node pool. Not universal but mostly nodes on updated pool.
Lucas: quick datapoint: tcpdump on node shows lots of fragmented VXLAN packets and retransmits when streams stall. PMTU sysctl looks default (1500) but encapsulation adds overhead.
Taylor: can you paste the tcpdump snippet?
aj: snippet below (truncated):
```
15:03:12.123456 IP (tos 0x0, ttl 63, id 54321, offset 0, flags [DF]) 10.2.1.5.50000 > 10.3.2.9.60000: Flags [.], seq 1:1401, ack 1, win 65535, length 1400
15:03:12.123462 IP (frag 1) 10.2.1.5 > 10.3.2.9: frag 0: df set, offset 1480
...
```
Maria: that looks like GSO/GRO offload interacting badly with VXLAN fragmentation. Recent driver change can expose that.
sre-bot: Incident detected: grpc_streaming_error_rate > 3% for service gpu-inference (us-west-2).
Lucas: iPerf between nodes shows MTU drop when VXLAN enabled:
```
iperf3 -c 10.3.2.9 -M 9000
[  5] local 10.2.1.5 port 50000 connected to 10.3.2.9 port 5201
No MTU discovery: sending smaller segments
```
Taylor: Are RDMA jobs affected? we have some RDMA-backed transfer for checkpointing.
aj: interestingly RDMA flows are fine — they bypass the overlay. This seems limited to encapsulated pod-to-pod traffic (vxlan/gso path).
Maria: hypothesis: NIC firmware updated changed GSO hw offload semantics; kernel tried to send large segments across VXLAN causing fragmentation that PMTU discovery doesn't handle due to SNAT / iptables conntrack dropping ICMP unreachable.
Lucas: confirmed: iptables MASQUERADE on egress chain is dropping ICMP frag-needed in our setup. PMTU blackhole for encapsulated flows.
Taylor: quick workaround?
aj: we tested two short-term options: 1) disable TX GSO for vxlan interfaces (sysctl net.ipv4.conf.all.gso_disabled=1) OR 2) reduce veth MTU to 1400 to account for encap. Disabling GSO fixed stalls in canary.
Maria: pros/cons: disabling GSO increases CPU usage and reduces throughput but immediate fix. MTU reduce is safer but requires rolling live pods and CNI update.
sre-bot: Recommended action: patch CNI to set pod MTU to 1400 for affected node pools and rollout.
devops-oncall: I'll open a runbook: set pod MTU, patch CNI config, and add iptables rule to allow ICMP frag-needed for conntrack. Also planning NIC rollback for oldest firmware on 2 nodes to validate.
Taylor: who owns the rollout?
devops-oncall: ops will run the CNI change for west pool tonight at 22:00 UTC, canary 10% nodes first. aj to validate gRPC stream health.
aj: I'll validate with long-lived load test and post logs. For longer term we should: 1) enforce conntrack/ICMP handling for PMTU, 2) coordinate firmware changes with offload semantics, 3) add unit test in cluster e2e that simulates vxlan + GSO.
Lucas: noted — I'll add a check in prow to verify VXLAN + GSO interactions on upgrades.
Maria: thanks everyone. tagging @Taylor for downstream GPU scheduling impact once fixed. :thumbsup:
Taylor: ack, will update capacity planning if we see sustained GPU backlog.
aj: posting follow-up after canary tonight.
